newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-AUXERRE, PSG BOOST MORALE FOR EUROPEAN BATTLES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUXERRE, PSG BOOST MORALE FOR EUROPEAN BATTLES.

text.p: Monaco succumbed to Auxerre's tight marking in their weekend league clash but they can take heart from the knowledge that they will have more space in their next home game against Newcastle.
"It was a very difficult match for us," coach Jean Tigana said after the 0-0 at the Louis II stadium on Sunday night.
"With the duels that Auxerre's players imposed on us it was very difficult to get out of this trap."
All three of Tigana's chief attacking players, Brazilian Anderson, teenager Thierry Henry and playmaker Ali Benarbia, were man-marked by Auxerre's uncompromising back three.
Monaco are away to Rennes on Thursday before the home leg of their UEFA Cup quarter-final against Newcastle the following Tuesday -- they hold a 1-0 lead from the first leg in Newcastle last week.
Auxerre are preparing for European Cup survival. They host Borussia Dortmund on March 19, 3-1 down from the first leg in Germany, after the home league game against Cannes on Friday.
France's other European contenders Paris St Germain boosted their morale with a first home win for four months, 3-1 against Lyon, to climb within four points of Monaco in second place.
PSG are away to AEK Athens in the second leg of their Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final after being held 0-0 at the Parc des Princes on Thursday. They are away to Le Havre in the league on Friday.

Defending league champions Auxerre have scored just one goal in their last six matches in all competitions. But they could have left Monaco with three points had Lilian Laslandes put away the best chance of the match early in the second half.
Tigana, watching the match from the stands as he began a four-game suspension for insulting a referee in January, was unhappy with the treatment his forwards received from the Auxerre defenders.
"The match this evening confirms what I said before the game about the refereeing," said Tigana, who had predicted Auxerre's tight marking and that the match officials would be lax.

"There were quite a few fouls that weren't punished and I'm surprised that Taribo West managed to finish the match. That makes me a bit angry," he said, referring to the Nigerian who used his arms a great deal marking the tricky Henry.
Both Tigana and Roux said their players had not fully recovered from their midweek European efforts.

"I'm satisfied with the score because it was an after-Europe match for both teams who showed a lot of fatigue," said Roux who will be on the bench for his 50th European match for the visit of Borussia Dortmund.
Auxerre captain Franck Silvestre said: "It was important for us after Dortmund to have such a performance against the leaders."
Silvestre could miss the return against Dortmund after injuring his knee on Sunday and this could let in Australian libero Ned Zelic who spent three seasons at the German club.
The Monaco match marked the return after a six-month absence of Zelic who injured his knee on September 16 at Nancy. He came on at the start of the second half for Silvestre.
